summary: Wire the demo app's (ye-olde-magic-shop) Playwright suite to the already-built, already-verified Saturday runner image (containers/saturday-runner/, debian target) so the map/Cesium tests run headed in real Chrome under Xvfb with software WebGL (ANGLE SwiftShader), instead of Playwright's bundled Chromium which cannot provide a WebGL context the way this suite needs. A first attempt was killed at a stage timeout mid-build and left working drafts on commit 034adbd (branch salvage/ui-suite-real-chrome): apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/playwright.config.ts (new 'chrome' project), apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/tests/webgl.spec.ts (webgl2 context assertion), scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh (build/run/health-check/runner-check/suite/report orchestration), a package.json test:chrome script, and a .dockerignore fix so the app's own lib/ source directory isn't excluded from the Docker build context. This order verifies and finishes those drafts against the acceptance criteria rather than rewriting them from scratch; it does not touch the runner image itself.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: playwright.config.ts MUST define a 'chrome' project with channel 'chrome', headless false, and launch args --use-gl=angle --use-angle=swiftshader, and the container MUST run that project. The bundled-Chromium 'chromium' project MUST remain for local runs. The chrome project's slowMo and video MUST come from environment variables and default to off.

scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh, run from the repo root on a machine with Docker, MUST build the image from containers/saturday-runner/Containerfile with --platform linux/amd64 --target debian without changing that Containerfile, mount the checkout at /work with a named pnpm store volume, install dependencies with --frozen-lockfile, start the app and the mock API, run runner-check and then the chrome project in that order, copy the Playwright report to artifacts/ui-suite/, and exit with the suite's exit code. The app and mock API MUST make no request off the container after dependencies are installed.

tests/webgl.spec.ts MUST assert a webgl2 context is available on the running app's page, and MUST fail when the browser is launched with --disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer added to the chrome project's launch args. That launch MUST be used once as a test-of-the-test and the result recorded in the delivery record.

If the image fails to build, or the app is not healthy within 180 seconds, the script MUST exit non-zero and state which of the two happened, using an exit code and message distinct from a Playwright test failure's exit code.

.dockerignore's bare 'lib' pattern MUST no longer exclude apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/lib/ from the Docker build context, without removing that pattern's effect on other lib/ directories (e.g. package build output).

Every new or changed function MUST have cyclomatic complexity below 7, every changed line MUST be covered by a test that can fail, and no file outside scope.paths MUST change, except this run's own delivery record under docs/features/ui-suite-real-chrome/.

nonFunctionalRequirements.requirement: The app and mock API must report healthy before the suite starts running against them; amd64 emulation on Apple Silicon is slow, so the budget is generous.

With RUNNER_VIEWER unset, the container must listen on no port; scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh must never set RUNNER_VIEWER and must never print the VNC viewer's password, even though the script never touches the viewer today.
The app and mock API processes must make no network request off the container after pnpm install completes (no telemetry, no package re-fetch mid-run).

proposedFitnessFunctions.verification: QA test asserting the resolved project config (e.g. `npx playwright test --project=chrome --list` or a small Node script reading the exported config) matches these fields.

proposedFitnessFunctions.verification: Shell-level test (e.g. stubbing docker/build/health-check calls) exercising each failure branch and asserting its exit code and stderr message.

proposedFitnessFunctions.property: tests/webgl.spec.ts passes under the chrome project's normal launch args and fails when --disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer is added to those args.
proposedFitnessFunctions.verification: Manual run of both variants inside the runner container; both outputs recorded in docs/features/ui-suite-real-chrome/. Not continuously run in CI, since it requires mutating launch args by hand.

proposedFitnessFunctions.property: .dockerignore no longer excludes apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/lib/ from the build context, and no earlier broader pattern re-excludes a parent directory of that path.
proposedFitnessFunctions.verification: Build the image and confirm apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/lib/site/*.ts exist inside the build context/container (or a .dockerignore-semantics unit test).

proposedFitnessFunctions.verification: Local run of both npm scripts on a developer machine without Xvfb; recorded as a regression check.

proposedFitnessFunctions.property: Cyclomatic complexity below 7 for every new/changed function; changed lines covered by a test that can fail.

The polyglot target (JDK, Python, Gradle, Go) — order runner-image-polyglot.

Changing any existing test's behaviour (assertions in map.spec.ts, cart.spec.ts, magic-shop.spec.ts, heatmap.spec.ts, example.spec.ts stay as-is).
Wiring scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh into .claude/delivery-policy.yaml's preShipChecks — spec states a human does this after merge; not part of this pipeline run.

Updating DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md for the spec's 'Runner image' term — that term is pre-existing infrastructure vocabulary already authoritatively defined in docs/runner-image.md (itself out of scope), not a new business concept this spec introduces, and DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md is outside scope.paths.

crossings: containers/saturday-runner (the runner image) — read-only dependency; this order consumes runner-check and the image's launch-arg contract without modifying the image.

affectedComponents.reason: Add the 'chrome' project (channel, headless, ANGLE/SwiftShader launch args, env-driven slowMo/video) alongside the existing 'chromium' project; verify default (no --project) runs don't pick up the headed chrome project locally.
Add a test:chrome script (`playwright test --project=chrome`) consistent with existing test:e2e/test:pw/test:bdd scripts.
New spec asserting a webgl2 context exists on the running app's page; must be provably able to fail (AC3).
New script: builds the image, mounts the repo, installs deps, starts app+mock-api, waits for health, runs runner-check then the chrome project, copies the report, and propagates the right exit code.
Un-exclude apps/ye-olde-magic-shop/lib/ from the bare 'lib' pattern so the Site-Centric pattern classes under it are present in the Docker build context.
Permanent delivery record: AC3's test-of-the-test evidence, AC4's negative-path evidence, and the end-to-end script run's output.

architecturalFlags: Purely additive within established patterns (new Playwright project, new spec file, new shell script matching scripts/update-framework.sh's conventions, a one-line .dockerignore fix) — no new package, base class, or layer-boundary change. Architect can be skipped.

No auth/API/input/secret-handling code is added, so security-reviewer is not strictly required by CLAUDE.md's trigger list — but the spec carries an explicit Trust Boundaries section about the VNC viewer's password. A short security-reviewer pass confirming scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh never sets RUNNER_VIEWER and never echoes the viewer's password is cheap insurance, even though the script as drafted never touches the viewer at all.

edgeCases.case: Default `playwright test` invocation (no --project flag) would, without guarding, resolve both the existing 'chromium' project and the new headed 'chrome' project.
edgeCases.handling: Scope project selection so npm run test:e2e / test:pw keep exercising only 'chromium' by default; 'chrome' runs only via --project=chrome or scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh. Otherwise local dev machines without a display, or CI machines without the Chrome channel installed, would start failing a previously-working script.

edgeCases.case: RUNNER_SLOW_MO is set to a non-numeric value.
edgeCases.handling: Number(process.env.RUNNER_SLOW_MO ?? 0) would resolve to NaN and get passed to Playwright's slowMo launch option; validate or default safely instead of passing NaN through.

edgeCases.case: runner-check fails inside the container (WebGL genuinely unavailable in the image).
edgeCases.handling: The 034adbd draft exits 1 here, the same value a generic Playwright test failure is likely to use. AC4 only requires distinctness for 'build failed' and 'app unhealthy', so this isn't a blocking gap, but developer should consider a dedicated exit code for clearer diagnosis.

edgeCases.case: Apple Silicon amd64 emulation slows image build and app startup.
edgeCases.handling: Keep the full 180s health-check budget (already generous per docs/runner-image.md's own build record); do not shorten it to speed up local iteration.

edgeCases.case: The app's existing map view fetches real map tiles from tile.openstreetmap.org client-side at /locations.
edgeCases.handling: Pre-existing behavior, unrelated to this order (out of scope: changing any existing test's behaviour) and not what AC2's 'app and mock API make no request off the container' governs — that clause is about the app/mock-api server processes, not browser-initiated page requests. Note as a known source of flakiness if the chrome project runs offline, but do not change it here.

edgeCases.case: The app process crashes shortly after starting, rather than just being slow to become healthy.
edgeCases.handling: The health-check polling loop in the 034adbd draft can't distinguish 'slow' from 'crashed' — both fall through to the same 180s timeout and the same tail -n 50 of the app log printed to stderr, which is sufficient for AC4's 'says which' requirement (distinct from a build failure).

edgeCases.case: The spec's Domain Language section defines 'Runner image', which would normally trigger a DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md update under the analyst's Ubiquitous Language rule.
edgeCases.handling: Skip: DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md is outside this order's scope.paths, and 'Runner image' is pre-existing infrastructure vocabulary already canonically defined in docs/runner-image.md (also out of scope), not a new concept this spec introduces.

definitionOfDone: All six acceptance criteria verified with evidence captured under docs/features/ui-suite-real-chrome/.
scripts/ui-suite-in-chrome.sh runs end-to-end against a real Docker daemon and exits 0 on a green suite.
webgl.spec.ts is proven to fail under --disable-gpu --disable-software-rasterizer and to pass under the normal chrome-project launch args; both runs recorded.
Existing suite's assertions are unchanged; npm run test:e2e / test:pw continue to work locally without attempting the headed chrome project.
Cyclomatic complexity below 7 and the ADR-008 coverage threshold (>=85% of changed lines) are met for every new/changed function.
No file outside scope.paths changed, except this run's own delivery record under docs/features/ui-suite-real-chrome/.
openQuestions: Should a runner-check failure inside the container get its own distinct exit code (separate from a Playwright test-failure exit code), the same way build-failure and app-unhealthy already do? AC4 names only the latter two cases; this is a judgment call for the developer/human.

Should the default `playwright test` project list (no --project flag) ever include 'chrome', or should local/default runs stay chromium-only until a human explicitly runs the container script? AC1's 'may stay for local runs' phrasing implies the latter, but the spec doesn't say so directly.
